## Water and wastewater treatment operator — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Operate treatment processes in responsible charge so that delivered water and discharged effluent meet their limits.

*X4 match:* `skos:closeMatch` (confidence 0.75, applies to: water treatment; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulated-party.

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* Drinking water treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV / Class A-D, state-specific) (required); Wastewater treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV) (required)

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band WG grade set by the federal wage system job grading standard (entry/journey/senior/lead) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Operate drinking water treatment processes to meet water quality targets**
  - Adjust coagulant dosing from jar test results when raw-water turbidity, temperature or organic content changes
  - Verify disinfection contact time against required inactivation values at each operating flow and correct shortfalls before water enters distribution
  - Respond to a treatment upset by isolating the affected process unit, bringing backup treatment online and notifying the primacy agency
  - Supervise automated process-control loops, overriding setpoints when analyzer readings conflict with bench tests or visual plant checks
- **Operate wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes to permit limits**
  - Adjust aeration and sludge wasting rates using solids inventory, settleability and dissolved-oxygen trends to hold effluent within permit limits
  - Diagnose a biological process upset from microscopic examination, foam, odor and settling behavior before laboratory results confirm it
  - Route peak wet-weather flows through the plant to protect biological treatment, recording any bypass or overflow for required reporting
  - Operate anaerobic digestion and solids handling to meet biosolids pathogen-reduction and stability requirements while recovering digester gas
- **Practice within licensure scope and responsible charge**
  - Determine whether an assigned task falls within the scope of one's licence or certification, referring out-of-scope work to a qualified professional
  - Exercise responsible charge over subordinates' professional work, directing and reviewing it so that the sealing professional can attest to it
- **Supervise automated and AI-assisted process control in environmental operations**
  - Run a treatment process in safe manual operation when automation or communications fail, adapting the manual operating procedure to conditions
  - Monitor automated control loops and alarms on a treatment process, checking automated responses against field observations of process condition
  - Override an automated control action when process indicators show it is driving the system toward a permit or safety limit, documenting the decision
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control**
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them
  - Report field conditions that invalidate samples, such as broken seals, temperature excursions or holding-time breaches, before results are used
- **Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites**
  - Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them
  - Isolate an incidentally discovered hazardous material, establishing a safe distance and notifying the designated responder before any further work
  - Wear the personal protective equipment the site health and safety plan specifies, checking its fit and function before entering the exclusion zone
- **Protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities**
  - Maintain an inventory of connected control and monitoring assets with their network zone, remote-access paths and owner.
  - Run an incident-response drill that switches a plant or monitoring network to manual operation, recording the time to a safe state and the gaps found.
  - Review remote access to control and monitoring systems under the change procedure, removing access that is no longer needed.
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings**
  - Conduct a no-blame review of a near miss or incident with the people involved to identify contributing conditions and corrective actions
  - Deliver a pre-work safety briefing that covers site hazards, controls, communications and the stop-work procedure for the assigned work area
  - Design a unit learning-from-incidents process that links reporting channels, review triggers and pre-work briefing content
- **Manage a municipal stormwater programme to meet permit conditions**
  - Inspect catch basins, pipes and outfalls on a scheduled route, recording each structure that restricts flow for cleaning
  - Trace an illicit discharge from a dry-weather outfall flow to its source using field screening and system maps

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language; target levels are editorial drafts)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: operate drinking water treatment processes to meet water quality targets (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: operate wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes to permit limits (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: supervise automated and AI-assisted process control in environmental operations (EMST target journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: practice within licensure scope and responsible charge (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage field sample custody and field quality control (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage a municipal stormwater programme to meet permit conditions (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: engineer environmental sensor-network and streaming data pipelines (EMST target senior L2, lead L3, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: validate AI-generated work products before professional use (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: record provenance and AI involvement in work products (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, senior L1, lead L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage physical assets and capital plans with risk-based asset management (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4, editorial draft).
